panels.title: Compile success rate (last 30m)
panels.description: Share of compile requests that returned READY_FOR_APPROVAL. Healthy: >70% on a clean dataset. Drops mean the model is rejecting or asking for clarification more often — investigate via the violations panel and the rejections/clarifications timeline.

panels.title: Compile p95 latency
panels.description: 95th-percentile end-to-end compile latency. Healthy: <30s for Claude Haiku / Gemini Flash. Spikes usually mean LLM API slowness — cross-check the LLM latency panel.

panels.title: Avg repair loops
panels.description: Average repair iterations per compile. Healthy: <1.0 (most plans valid on first try). Rising trend means the planner is making more safety-violating choices — the model may be drifting or the prompt is no longer aligned. Hard cap is 3 before REJECTED.

panels.title: LLM error rate (last 30m)
panels.description: Share of LLM calls returning rate_limited or error. Healthy: 0%. >0 → likely quota exhaustion or upstream LLM outage. Cross-reference with `mts_llm_calls_total{outcome="rate_limited"}`.

panels.title: Compile rate by final status
panels.description: Requests per second, broken out by status. READY/REJECTED/NEEDS_CLARIFICATION/error. A sudden REJECTED spike often means the safety-kernel is catching real planner regressions; an `error` spike means the LLM provider is failing.

panels.title: Compile latency p50/p95/p99
panels.description: Three percentiles over 5-minute windows. p50 is typical user experience; p95 is the worst common case; p99 is tail outliers. The gap between p50 and p99 is your variance.

panels.title: LLM calls per second (by outcome)
panels.description: Volume of LLM API calls split by ok/error/rate_limited. Should track 1:1 with compile rate (we make ~1 LLM call per attempt + 1 per repair). Big multiplier means the repair loop is hammering the LLM.

panels.title: LLM call latency p50/p95
panels.description: Single-LLM-call latency. Slower than ~5s p95 means the upstream LLM is under load or the prompt has grown. Most of the compile-latency budget is spent here.

panels.title: Safety-kernel violations (top checks)
panels.description: Which safety checks fire most often. Diagnostic: if `sensor_coverage_adequate` dominates, the planner is mislabeling perimeter patrols as SEARCH_PATTERN. If `avoids_nfz` dominates, the planner is ignoring NFZs. If `battery_within_budget` dominates, plans are too ambitious.

panels.title: Repair loops distribution (heatmap-ish)
panels.description: Histogram quantiles of repair-loop counts. p50=0 = clean planner; p95>1 = chronic struggle; p95=3 = planner failing → most calls REJECTED.

panels.title: Plan shape — legs per plan
panels.description: Distribution of plan complexity in legs. Most missions are 2–3 legs (work + RTB). A sudden shift to many legs may mean the planner is over-decomposing simple commands.

panels.title: Plan shape — estimated battery (%)
panels.description: Estimated battery consumption per approved plan. Helpful for tuning the drone profile + understanding mission realism. If p95 hits 80%, the planner is regularly cutting it close to the 20% reserve.

panels.title: Plan shape — estimated flight duration
panels.description: Estimated wall-clock flight time per approved plan. Useful as a sanity check: a 5-min perimeter patrol shouldn't suddenly become 30-min plans without a reason.
